entryPoint: SLA::addGracePeriod(Datetime $date, BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null, &$timeline = array()) in include/class.sla.php (line 47) — advances $date by the SLA's grace period, using business-hours math when a schedule resolves, else plain elapsed hours.
coreLogic: Two computation branches performed inline in SLA::addGracePeriod: (1) schedule-based path — calls $schedule->addWorkingHours($date, $this->getGracePeriod(), $timeline) (BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours in include/class.schedule.php:475), which itself constructs `new BusinessHours($this)` and delegates to BusinessHours::addWorkingHours($date, $hours, &$auditlog) in include/class.businesshours.php:87 (sets date's timezone to the schedule's timezone, logs to an internal timeline/auditlog, returns false if the schedule has zero entries, otherwise walks business-hours segments and returns the advanced DateTime or false); the schedule's timeline is captured back via BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours's own $timeline out-param. (2) No-schedule fallback path — inline math only: $time = round($this->getGracePeriod()*3600); $interval = new DateInterval('PT'.$time.'S'); $date->add($interval); return $date. Supporting getters used for orchestration (not part of the extracted core math): SLA::getSchedule() (lazy-loads $this->_schedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) if not already set) and SLA::getGracePeriod() (returns $this->grace_period).
consumers: Ticket::getSLADueDate($recompute=false) in include/class.ticket.php:547-563 — the only call site of SLA::addGracePeriod. It resolves $sla=$this->getSLA(), checks $sla->isActive(), gets $schedule=$this->getDept()->getSchedule(), builds a DateTime $dt in the DB timezone from getReopenDate() ?: getCreateDate(), calls $dt = $sla->addGracePeriod($dt, $schedule) (line 558), then re-normalizes $dt->setTimezone($tz) and returns $dt->format('Y-m-d H:i:s'). Relies on addGracePeriod both mutating $dt in place and returning it (the return value is reassigned but is the same mutated object).
inputShape: Datetime $date (required, mutated in place by reference semantics of PHP objects — no clone is made by the caller or the method); BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null (optional; if omitted the method falls back to $this->getSchedule() then $cfg->getDefaultSchedule()); &$timeline = array() (optional by-reference out-param, populated with a business-hours audit/timeline log only when the schedule path executes; left as the caller's empty array on the no-schedule fallback path). Grace period hours are read from $this->getGracePeriod() (the SLA's own grace_period column), not passed as a parameter.
outputShape: Returns the same Datetime object passed in as $date, advanced forward by the grace period (schedule-based business-hours advance, or a flat DateInterval of getGracePeriod()*3600 seconds). The object is mutated in place; the return value is a convenience reference to that same mutated object, not a new instance. No explicit false/null return in the facade method itself (the underlying BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours/BusinessHours::addWorkingHours can return false internally, but the facade's `if (($schedule->addWorkingHours(...)))` guard only branches on truthiness to decide whether to `return $date` early — it does not propagate a false back to SLA::addGracePeriod's own caller).
sideEffects: Reads global $cfg (via `global $cfg;`) and calls $cfg->getDefaultSchedule(), which lazily loads and caches $cfg->defaultSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($cfg->getDefaultScheduleId()) — a DB read on first access, memoized on the $cfg object for the request.

Calls $this->getSchedule() when no schedule is passed, which lazily loads and caches $this->_schedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) — a DB read on first access per SLA instance.

When the schedule path runs, BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours constructs `new BusinessHours($this)` (a fresh object per call, no caching) and calls BusinessHours::addWorkingHours, which mutates the passed-in $date's timezone via $date->setTimezone($this->getSchedule()->getDatetimeZone()) as a side effect on the caller's DateTime object, and appends timeline/audit-log entries (via an internal $this->timeline(...) call and the &$auditlog out-param) that are surfaced back through the &$timeline reference parameter of addGracePeriod.
Mutates the caller-supplied Datetime $date object in place (both branches) rather than returning a new DateTime instance.
Populates the by-reference &$timeline argument in the schedule path (business-hours segment log); leaves it unchanged (still the caller's default empty array) on the no-schedule fallback path.
No direct DB writes, file I/O, or caching beyond the lazy-load memoization on $cfg and the SLA instance described above.
constraints: Schedule precedence order must be preserved exactly: requested $schedule parameter first, then $this->getSchedule() (the SLA's own configured schedule), then $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (system default) — first truthy value wins, short-circuit `?:` chain.

If no schedule resolves from any of the three sources (all null/false), or if the resolved schedule's addWorkingHours() call returns falsy, execution must fall through to the plain-hours fallback (round(getGracePeriod()*3600) seconds added via DateInterval) rather than returning early.
When a schedule resolves AND $schedule->addWorkingHours() returns truthy, the method must return immediately with $date from that branch — it must not also apply the flat-hours fallback afterward.

The by-reference &$timeline parameter must continue to be populated only via the schedule/business-hours path, matching current behavior (BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours assigns $timeline = $bhrs->getTimeline() only in that call path).

$date must remain the same object identity throughout — callers depend on in-place mutation (Ticket::getSLADueDate reassigns $dt = $sla->addGracePeriod($dt, $schedule) but then continues to use $dt, so a new/cloned DateTime instance would still work here, but any extraction must not silently drop the in-place mutation semantics other undiscovered callers might rely on).

Grace period value must come from $this->getGracePeriod() (the SLA's own grace_period field) at call time — not memoized before the schedule resolution logic runs, since schedule resolution does not modify grace_period, but the read order relative to schedule resolution should be preserved for clarity/parity.

The flat-hours fallback must use round($this->getGracePeriod() * 3600) seconds (not a raw/unrounded value) inside a DateInterval string 'PT<seconds>S' — rounding behavior must be preserved exactly for parity.

Method signature `addGracePeriod(Datetime $date, BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null, &$timeline = array())` must remain unchanged after extraction; SLA::addGracePeriod becomes a thin delegating wrapper per the strangler pattern (facade keeps globals/$cfg access and schedule-precedence orchestration; only the core grace-period math is extracted).

Per the anti-recursion rule, the extracted service must not call back into SLA::addGracePeriod — it should only perform the lifted math/delegate to BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours / plain DateInterval logic, not re-enter the facade.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with: start (string, ISO 8601 datetime); hours (number, grace period hours — use 0 for guard cases); schedule_id (integer, BusinessHoursSchedule id — 1 for normal business-hours schedule, 5 for empty-schedule fallback testing)
